 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-

That on 24-06-2024, at about 09-30 A.M., the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP- 26-AQ-1324 on Chowdepalle-Palamaner road and when he reached infront of Cricket Ground, near Dadepalle village, Chittoor, A.P, at that time the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.AP-39-GH-6457 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Apollo Hospital, Chittoor wherein admitted as an inpatient for 23 days.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 62 years.
He was doing Coolie work and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/the RC owner of JCB bearing Reg.No.AP-39-GH- 6457 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex- parte.

5. The respondent No.2 /the Insurer of JCB bearing Reg.No.AP-39-GH-6457 has filed written statement and contended that the JCB vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle in order to have unlawful gain and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner who was not holding valid driving license and that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the JCB and the driver of the JCB was not holding valid driving license.
The respondent no.2 has further contended that there is four days delay in lodging the complaint.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 24-06-2024 at about 9-30 a.m., infront of Cricket Ground, on Venkatappa M vs Vediyappan S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109212933/
2 Chowdepalle -Palamaner road, Dadepalle village, Chittoor, Andra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.AP-39-GH-6457 ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as Pw.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

The respondent no.2 has examined Assistant of the 2nd respondent as RW.1 and later on her evidence was discarded and examined the Deputy Manager of respondent no.2 company as RW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.,
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P3 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, translated copy of FIR with complaint, wound certificate, charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri M V Padmavathi, case has been registered against the driver of alleged offending vehicle in Crime No.110/2024 of Chowdepalle Police Station for the offence punishable under section 337 of IPC.
After completing investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the alleged offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 338, 337 of IPC.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 in its written statement so also in the evidence has disputed the very involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident and contended that the petitioner has falsely implicated the alleged offending vehicle in the accident in collusion with the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and police officials hence only complaint was lodged after four days of the alleged accident.
Hence, submitted to dismiss the petition on that ground itself.

14. In the light of the serious objection raised by the respondent no.2 regarding involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident, if the materials placed on record is perused, the accident in question has occurred on 24-06-2024 at about 9-30 pm,.
The complaint came to be lodged by the daughter of the petitioner on 28-06-2024.
Hence, there is a delay of four days in lodging the complaint.
It is true that in the complaint the complainant has stated that she was engaged in providing treatment for her father hence complaint was lodged after 4 days of the accident.

The petitioner who got examined as PW.1 in his cross examination has deposed that after the accident he lost his conscious and he was in the ICU for a period of 3 days and that in the Apollo hospital at Chittoor they have given information as to the history of accident.
If the Discharge summary produced by the petitioner is perused, no where it is stated that petitioner was unconscious while his admitted to the hospital.

As per the case of the petitioner, soon after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital Palamaner and from there he was shifted to Government Hospital Chittoor and from there he was shifted to Apollo hospital at Chittoor.

Though the respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of alleged offending vehicle in the accident but the petitioner has failed to produce MLC register maintained in the aforesaid 3 hospital to let the Court know whether petitioner was admitted in the hospital on the history of RTA hit by JCB/alleged offending vehicle.
When PW.1 has stated that they have given information regarding history of injury sustained by him at Apollo hospital at Chittoor, nothing prevented the petitioner from producing the MLC register.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, on the date of accident he was proceeding in Chowdepalli/
Palameneru road and when he reached Dadepalle Village, the alleged offending vehicle came from opposite direction in a wrong way and hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
At the risk of repetition, the respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

Even if the respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident in tooth and nail but leaving apart of producing MLC register, the petitioner even has not produced spot mahazar, sketch, IMV Report, Notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given by the owner of the alleged offending vehicle to the said notice.
The petitioner has not produced primary and material documents above referred before the court to prove that the alleged offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

Mere producing charge sheet before the court would not suffice to prove the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident so also the rash and negligent act on the part of the alleged offending vehicle.

16. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 during the course of cross examination of PW.1 has posed specific suggestion that since the alleged accident in question has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, in order to suppress the said fact before the court, the petitioner intentionally has not produced the spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report before the court.
It is relevant to state here that the PW.1 has admitted the said suggestion.

If really offending vehicle was involved in the accident or if really accident in question was occurred due to the rash and negligent Venkatappa M vs Vediyappan S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109212933/

4 driving of the alleged offending vehicle, even after the counsel for respondent no.2 has posed suggestions to the aforesaid effect, the petitioner could have produced the said material documents before the court.

Hence the very defence taken by the respondent no.2 disputing the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and the very act of the petitioner not producing MLC register,
spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Notice and reply u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act which would create doubt in the mind of the court about the genuineness of the case put forward by the petitioner.

Had the petitioner produced the MLC, spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report it would have thrown light on the case of the petitioner in proving the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident,
so also the rash and negligent driving of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident.
If really alleged offending vehicle i.e., JCB has hit to the vehicle of the petitioner then definitely some amount of damages would have been caused to the motor cycle of the petitioner so also JCB.
If petitioner had produced IMV Report, it could have been assessed by the court regarding the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident.

The mere production of FIR, complaint,
wound certificate, charge sheet and discharge summary would not sufficient to prove the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident and the rash and negligent driving of the alleged offending vehicle.

Hence without discussing much on this point considering the fact that there is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint and that petitioner has failed to produce MLC register, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply on the said notice, case sheet and inpatient record etc., this court is of the opinion that petitioner has not approached the court with clean hands to claim compensation.
Hence petitioner is not entitled for relief as claimed by him.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
17. Issue No.2:-
As petitioner had failed to prove the very involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, the question of discussing issue no.2 does not arise.
Hence, issue no.2 is also answered in the negative.
18. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 6th day of November 2025.)
